name: Kochi
summary: Chinese fishing nets, old trading streets and a waterfront shaped by centuries of exchange.
look: Along the Fort Kochi waterfront, fishing nets rise against the sky. In Mattancherry, narrow streets lead past spice warehouses, tiled roofs and historic buildings. The city’s character shifts between quiet heritage quarters and a busy modern harbour.
history: Kochi grew into an important Indian Ocean trading port during the medieval period. Its trade connected Kerala with merchants from Arabia, China and beyond. Portuguese, Dutch and later British influence left traces in the city’s architecture, while long-established local communities shaped its food, faith and everyday life.
highlights: Fort Kochi waterfront
Walk along the shore to see the Chinese fishing nets and watch the harbour change through the day.
Mattancherry & Jew Town
Explore a neighbourhood known for spice trading, historic lanes and the Paradesi Synagogue. Check visiting hours and local customs.
Mattancherry Palace
Discover the former royal palace, known for its Kerala murals and its connections to the Kochi royal family.
season: November to February is usually more comfortable for walking. The monsoon brings heavy showers and a different waterfront atmosphere.
tip: Make time for a waterfront walk early or late in the day, and ask before photographing people at work.

name: Kumarakom
intro: A quieter world by the water.
summary: A lakeside landscape of coconut palms, village waterways and birdlife around Vembanad.
look: Wide lake views open beyond green banks, coconut groves and smaller canals. Fishing boats move across the water, while narrow lanes connect homes and village life along the shore. Mornings can be especially atmospheric around the wetlands.
history: Kumarakom’s story is closely tied to Vembanad Lake and the communities that have relied on fishing, farming and water transport. Over time, the region became known to visitors for its backwater landscape and bird sanctuary. Traditional livelihoods remain an important part of the area’s character.
highlights: Vembanad Lake
Take in the broad lake landscape and the changing light across the water.
Kumarakom Bird Sanctuary
A wetland habitat known for resident and seasonal birds. Sightings vary with season and time of day.
Village waterways
Notice small canals, coconut palms and the daily connections between people and water.
season: The cooler months are generally pleasant. Bird activity varies by species and season; check locally before planning a sanctuary visit.
tip: Bring binoculars for birdwatching and keep voices low near wildlife. Water activities depend on weather and local conditions.

name: Alleppey
summary: Palm-lined canals, traditional houseboats and everyday life woven around the backwaters.
look: Alleppey brings together canals, lagoons, rice-growing landscapes and a town facing the Arabian Sea. Thatched-roof houseboats share the wider waterways with smaller local boats. Along the banks, homes and coconut palms create an ever-changing waterside scene.
history: Alappuzha developed as a port and trading centre under the Travancore kingdom in the late eighteenth century. Its canals helped move goods, and the town became associated with coir production. The large kettuvallam boats once used to carry cargo helped inspire the houseboats now associated with Kerala’s backwaters.
highlights: Backwater landscapes
See how canals, lakes and low-lying fields connect the wider region.
Traditional houseboats
Learn about the kettuvallam tradition and the relationship between boatbuilding and trade.
Alappuzha Beach
Spend time along the Arabian Sea shore and see the remains of the historic pier from the beach.
season: November to February is often comfortable. Monsoon weather can affect boat operations and visibility.
tip: Discuss boat routes and operator standards with your guide. Ask before photographing residents along the canals.

name: Munnar
intro: A little closer to the clouds.
summary: Tea-covered hills, winding roads and cool mountain landscapes in the Western Ghats.
look: Tea gardens trace the slopes in long green patterns, broken by wooded valleys and mist. The roads curve past viewpoints and small settlements. In the wider highlands, grassland and shola forest create a landscape quite different from Kerala’s coast.
history: Munnar has a history that includes Indigenous communities and the later expansion of plantations during the colonial period. Tea cultivation transformed much of the landscape and drew workers to the hills. The region’s present-day identity reflects both the plantation economy and the ecology of the Western Ghats.
highlights: Tea landscapes
Enjoy the hillside views and learn about the work behind tea production. Enter estates only where visitors are permitted.
Eravikulam National Park
A protected highland habitat associated with the Nilgiri tahr. Opening and access can change seasonally.
Mountain viewpoints
Follow the winding roads for valley views, changing cloud cover and a cooler side of Kerala.
season: Conditions are often pleasant outside the heaviest monsoon periods. Rain and mist can limit views, and protected areas may close seasonally.
tip: Bring a light layer and allow extra travel time on mountain roads. Stay on permitted paths in plantations and protected areas.

name: Thekkady
summary: Forested hills, spice-growing country and the lake landscape of the Periyar region.
look: The landscape around Thekkady is rich in green: wooded slopes, spice plants and the waters of Periyar Lake. Tree trunks rising from the lake form one of the area’s recognisable views. The nearby town of Kumily serves as a gateway to this part of the hills.
history: The Periyar landscape was reshaped by the Mullaperiyar dam in the late nineteenth century, which created the reservoir associated with today’s lake views. The area later developed a major conservation role as Periyar Wildlife Sanctuary and Tiger Reserve. The surrounding hills also have long connections with spice cultivation and trade.
highlights: Periyar lake landscape
See the forested shoreline and distinctive standing tree trunks. Activities operate under local reserve rules.
Spice-growing country
Learn how crops such as pepper and cardamom connect the region’s climate, farming and trading history.
Guided nature experiences
Ask about officially permitted walks and activities. Wildlife sightings are never guaranteed.
season: The cooler, drier months are often comfortable. Reserve access and activities depend on weather, conservation needs and current rules.
tip: Use official reserve activities, follow your naturalist’s instructions and never approach or feed wildlife.

name: Kovalam
intro: Follow the curve of the coast.
summary: A lighthouse headland, crescent-shaped beaches and palm-lined views over the Arabian Sea.
look: Kovalam’s coastline curves around rocky headlands into sheltered-looking bays. The red-and-white lighthouse rises above the palms, while fishing boats and beachside paths add colour along the shore. The sea changes from bright blue to silver as the light shifts.
history: Kovalam was a coastal fishing settlement before it became widely known as a visitor destination during the twentieth century. Its growing reputation was linked to the Travancore royal family’s association with the area and, later, international travel. Fishing communities remain part of the coast’s living identity.
highlights: Lighthouse Beach
See the landmark headland and the curve of the shore. Check current opening hours before visiting the lighthouse.
Coastal walks
Take in sea views from public paths, pausing to watch the changing light and the boats along the coast.
Life by the Arabian Sea
Learn about the area’s fishing traditions and how the coast shapes everyday life.
season: November to February is generally comfortable. Monsoon weather can bring rough seas and restrictions on water activities.
tip: Follow lifeguard instructions and warning flags. Do not assume a sheltered-looking bay is safe for swimming.
